beats.intro: In algebra, letters stand for numbers. [[q]]Put letters, numbers, and operations together, and you get an expression.
beats.define: An expression is a math phrase made of numbers, variables, and operations. [[var]]A variable is a letter that stands for a value, like x. [[ex]]Three x plus nine is an expression. [[ex2]]So are seven a squared minus four a b, and just thirty-eight m. [[no]]An expression has no equals sign: it's a phrase, not a sentence.
beats.terms: Expressions are built from terms. [[split]]Plus and minus signs split an expression into terms. [[ex]]Three x plus nine has two terms: three x, and nine. [[ex2]]Seven a squared minus four a b plus six has three terms. [[sign]]The sign in front belongs to the term, so the middle term is negative four a b.
beats.names: Expressions are named by how many terms they have. [[mono]]One term is a monomial: mono means one. [[bi]]Two terms make a binomial: bi means two. [[tri]]Three terms make a trinomial: tri means three. [[poly]]Any sum of such terms is a polynomial: poly means many.
beats.parts: Let's look inside a single term. [[term]]Take seven a squared. [[coef]]The number in front, seven, is the coefficient. [[var]]The letter a is the variable, [[exp]]and the small two is its exponent. [[one]]If no number is written, the coefficient is one: x squared means one times x squared. [[const]]A term with no variable at all, like nine, is called a constant.
beats.degree: The degree of a term is the sum of the exponents on its variables. [[t1]]Seven a squared has degree two. [[t2]]Four x cubed y squared has degree three plus two, five. [[t3]]Six a b has degree two, because a and b each have an unwritten exponent of one. [[t4]]A constant has degree zero. [[poly]]The degree of a polynomial is the highest degree of any of its terms: negative x squared plus two x minus five has degree two.
beats.q2: Quick check. Two questions about the parts of a term.
beats.standard: Standard form puts the terms in order, from the highest exponent down, with the constant last. [[q]]Take nine x squared minus four x plus five halves plus ten x cubed. [[find]]Ten x cubed has the highest exponent, so it moves to the front. [[move]]Then nine x squared, then negative four x, and the constant five halves goes last. [[sign]]Each term carries its sign with it: the four x is still subtracted.
beats.wrap: An expression combines numbers, variables, and operations. [[w1]]Plus and minus signs split it into terms, and each term keeps its sign. [[w2]]A term has a coefficient, variables, and exponents; the degree is the sum of the exponents. [[w3]]Standard form lists terms from the highest degree down. [[end]]Now try the chapter practice.
